title: Check yourself: When to escalate, and when not to

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer writes that they want to speak to a person about a change of delivery address. The agent has a tool that can make the change in one step. What should the agent do?

options.text: Hand over to a human straight away, before touching the account
options.says: An explicit request for a person is honoured at once, with no investigation first.

options.text: Make the change first, since it takes one step, then offer a transfer
options.says: Ruled out because "an investigation before the transfer is the agent deciding it knows better".

options.text: Ask why a human is wanted and transfer only if the reason is unclear
options.says: Ruled out because the agent "does not first try to solve the problem, ask why", and a question is a delay.

options.text: Offer to complete the update and transfer only if the customer repeats the wish
options.says: Ruled out because "An explicit request is honoured at once"; offering a fix first is the answer for frustration, not for a request.

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer asks the agent to match a competitor's lower price. The policy describes adjustments to the company's own prices and says nothing about competitors. The agent can issue a price adjustment. What should it do?

options.text: Apply the nearest own-price rule, as that is the fairest reading
options.says: Ruled out because "an agent that applies the nearest rule is inventing policy".

options.text: Decline politely, since the policy does not allow the match
options.says: Ruled out because "A policy exception or a gap is a trigger", and declining is also a decision the policy did not make.

options.text: Route it to a colleague authorised to rule on the exception
options.says: A silent policy is a gap, and a gap goes to a person who can decide.

options.text: Issue the adjustment and flag it for review afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because "the agent escalates and does not invent policy", and acting first leaves the invention in place.
